component.name: Apache Synapse
component.description: Lightweight, high-performance Enterprise Service Bus (ESB) / mediation engine. It accepts messages over pluggable transports (HTTP/S, JMS, VFS, Mail), runs them through operator-defined mediation sequences and proxy services (XSLT, XQuery, script, filter, switch, send-to-endpoint mediators), and routes/transforms them toward backend endpoints. The synapse configuration (sequences, mediators, scripts, XSLT/XQuery, endpoints, security policies) is trusted input authored by the integration developer; the inbound message from a network client is the untrusted adversary input. Modelled against master with dependency defaults verified against Axis2 1.7.9 and Axiom 1.2.22.

externalReferences.comment: Source security model document; this file is a structured translation of it. v1, source-verified, reviewed by the Synapse PMC.

blueprints.name: Synapse mediation deployment
blueprints.description: Synapse deployed as a message broker/mediator in front of or between services: clients send messages to a Synapse proxy/API; Synapse mediates (transform, route, secure, throttle) and forwards to backend endpoints. In message-mediation mode Synapse additionally acts as a WS-Addressing-style router: a bare <send/> with no configured endpoint forwards to the message's implicit To address. The trust boundary is the transport listener plus the mediation entry; bytes arriving on a listener are untrusted until mediation and any configured WS-Security/transport auth has processed them.

assets.name: Transport listeners
assets.description: HTTP/S (NHTTP/passthrough), JMS, VFS, and Mail listeners receiving untrusted messages from the network, filesystem, or mail.

assets.name: Mediation engine
assets.description: Sequences, proxy services, and APIs executing operator-defined mediation logic over inbound messages.

assets.name: XML transform mediators (XSLT, XQuery, payload factory)
assets.description: High-value surface: transform input is the already-parsed AXIOM tree; the TransformerFactory is created with JAXP defaults (FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING not set), so document()/doc() and extension functions remain available to the trusted stylesheet.

assets.name: Script mediators
assets.description: Operator-authored JS/Groovy code running over message data; the code is trusted config, the risk is unsafe handling of message data inside it.

assets.name: Outbound endpoints (send/call mediators)
assets.description: Network egress surface: address/WSDL/loadbalance endpoints, plus attacker-influenced routes via explicit dynamic/content-based routing and the implicit To routing of a bare <send/> in message-mediation mode (SSRF surface).

assets.name: Secure-vault secrets
assets.description: Encrypted configuration secrets kept under a keystore-backed asymmetric/symmetric cipher (org.apache.synapse.securevault); PasswordManager resolves encrypted passwords at runtime, plaintext only in memory at use.

zones.name: Message clients
zones.description: Any peer that can send a message to a Synapse listener, proxy, or API; untrusted.

zones.name: Synapse runtime
zones.description: The mediation engine, mediators, and operator-managed configuration, keystores, and transport setup on the JVM host.

zones.name: Backend endpoints
zones.description: Services Synapse calls; semi-trusted, their responses re-enter mediation.

persona.description: Untrusted primary adversary: crafts SOAP/XML/JSON payloads (oversized, deeply nested, malformed), supplies data that a trusted transform passes to external resolution, supplies To/routing values that mediation turns into outbound destinations (SSRF), or data that a script mishandles. DOCTYPE-based payloads (XXE, billion-laughs) are rejected at the build boundary by default.
Secondary adversary: a malicious backend returning hostile responses that re-enter mediation as semi-trusted input.
Authors the synapse config: mediation logic, scripts, XSLT, endpoints, secure-vault secrets, transport and WS-Security policy. Trusted; out of model as adversary.

assumptions.description: JVM host running the Synapse runtime; operator-managed synapse.xml config, keystores, and transport setup; TLS provided by the transport configuration.
Secure-vault secrets are protected by an operator-managed keystore and password.
Because there are no built-in message-size limits, deployment-level ingress controls (reverse proxy / load balancer request-size caps, connection limits) are assumed for internet-facing listeners.
The pinned Axis2/Axiom builder stack must not be downgraded or swapped for a builder that permits DOCTYPE; the default DOCTYPE rejection depends on it.

Reachability precondition: a finding is in-model if reachable from an inbound message before the mediation auth/validation the integration configured; a finding requiring a malicious config (script, XSLT body, endpoint address chosen by the operator) is out of model as trusted input.

threats.name: XXE or DTD entity expansion via inbound XML
threats.description: An entity defined via DOCTYPE in an inbound message being resolved or expanded on a default build path. Source-verified as blocked by default: both SOAP and POX build paths go through Axis2 BuilderUtil with Axiom StAXParserConfiguration.SOAP, whose StAXDialect.disallowDoctypeDecl rejects a DOCTYPE declaration outright, blocking classic XXE and DTD-based billion-laughs. No supported knob re-enables it per-service; a report reaching XXE through the default build path is VALID, and one reproduced only by re-enabling DOCTYPE support (custom builder, modified Axiom/StAX config, non-pinned dependency) is out of model as a non-default build. Critical severity.

threats.name: Crash or memory corruption from crafted messages
threats.description: Malformed inbound messages must yield a fault, not memory corruption; a crash or memory corruption (not mere resource exhaustion) from crafted input violates the robust message building property. High severity.

threats.name: Message content interpreted as stylesheet, query, or script code
threats.description: Stylesheets, XQuery bodies, and script bodies execute only from operator-loaded configuration, never from message content (source-verified: mediator factories read these from config/registry only). Message content being interpreted as stylesheet/query/script code is a critical violation.

threats.name: Bypass of configured mediation-level security
threats.description: An unauthenticated or forged message accepted where a configured transport-security or WS-Security (Rampart) policy required authentication, signature, or encryption. Enforcement is Rampart's; see the CXF/WSS4J sibling model for signature-wrapping classes. Critical severity.

threats.name: Exposure of configured secrets
threats.description: A plaintext secret in config at rest, or a secret emitted to logs by the framework, violates the secure-vault secret protection property. High severity. Secret exfiltration through an over-broad transform or log mediator is a known attack class for integrations to watch.

threats.name: Man-in-the-middle where TLS is expected
threats.description: TLS on HTTPS listeners and outbound calls with certificate validation is supported when configured; MITM where TLS is expected is a high-severity violation.

threats.name: SSRF via message-derived outbound destinations
threats.description: Synapse provides no intrinsic SSRF protection for message-derived destinations: both explicit dynamic/content-based routing built by the integration (header/XPath-derived addresses) and the designed-in implicit To routing of a bare <send/> in message-mediation mode (source-verified in SendMediator, no built-in allow-listing). Validating/allow-listing destinations is the integration's job; SSRF via implicit To routing is by-design disclaimed. A report showing it bypasses an explicitly configured endpoint or allow-list would be VALID.

threats.name: Resource exhaustion from oversized or deeply nested messages
threats.description: There are no built-in message-size, element-depth, or entity-count limits in the NHTTP/passthrough transports. Passthrough streaming plus deferred building bound the pure-routing path, but the moment a mediator reads the payload the full message is built with no size bound. Bounding oversized or deeply nested messages on parsing paths is a deployment responsibility; resource-exhaustion reports within input-proportional bounds against defaults are by-design disclaimed, unless they show asymmetric amplification beyond input size, which remains in model.

threats.name: External resolution via trusted transforms fed message data
threats.description: XSLT/XQuery transforms can read files or fetch URLs via document()/doc() (XQuery via Saxon XQJ) or extension functions, because FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING is not set by default. The stylesheet/query body is trusted config, so this becomes an attacker surface only when the operator's stylesheet feeds message-derived strings into resolution-capable constructs, an integration responsibility with a per-mediator hardening knob available.

threats.name: Unsafe handling of message data in operator scripts
threats.description: A script mediator looks sandboxed but runs with the engine's privileges; it is operator code, not a security boundary for message data. Routing untrusted message content into a script that executes or concatenates it unsafely is a known misuse pattern; the code itself is trusted config and Synapse offers no defence against the integration developer.

threats.name: Exposure of unsecured proxies
threats.description: A proxy with no transport or WS-Security configured is only as protected as the integration wired it; Synapse provides no security without configuration. Exposing a proxy with no security and assuming the ESB 'is secure' is a known misuse pattern.

trustBoundaries.name: Transport listener trust boundary
trustBoundaries.description: Bytes arriving on a listener are untrusted until mediation and any configured WS-Security/transport auth has processed them. The wire-to-message build transition rejects DOCTYPE by default; the passthrough transport defers building the body until a mediator needs it.

trustBoundaries.name: Outbound endpoint trust boundary
trustBoundaries.description: Static endpoints are trusted config; attacker-influenced routes exist through explicit content-based routing and implicit To routing. Backend responses re-enter mediation as semi-trusted input.

controls.name: DOCTYPE rejection on inbound XML
controls.description: SOAP and POX build paths use Axis2 BuilderUtil with Axiom StAXParserConfiguration.SOAP (StAXDialect.disallowDoctypeDecl): a DOCTYPE declaration in an inbound message is rejected outright, blocking classic XXE and DTD-based entity expansion by default. Versions pinned: Axis2 1.7.9, Axiom 1.2.22.

controls.name: Passthrough streaming and deferred message building
controls.description: The passthrough HTTP transport defers building the message body (RelayUtils/DeferredMessageBuilder): the envelope is only parsed when a mediator actually needs it, so pure-routing configurations never parse untrusted bodies at all. This bounds only untouched bodies, not parsing paths.

controls.name: Trusted-config-only transform and script code
controls.description: Mediator factories read stylesheets, XQuery bodies, and script bodies from operator-loaded configuration or registry only, never from message content.

controls.name: Secure-vault secret encryption
controls.description: Configured secrets are kept encrypted at rest under a keystore-backed asymmetric/symmetric cipher and resolved to plaintext only in memory at use (org.apache.synapse.securevault, PasswordManager).

controls.name: Configure transport security and WS-Security
controls.description: When configured, transport security and WS-Security (Rampart) authenticate, sign, and encrypt messages. Configure them where the integration requires authentication or integrity; use of a weak algorithm explicitly configured in a WS-Security policy is an integration choice.

controls.name: Configure transport TLS with certificate validation
controls.description: TLS on HTTPS listeners and outbound calls with certificate validation, configured by the operator for both inbound and outbound traffic.

controls.name: Deployment-level ingress limits
controls.description: Cap request sizes and connection counts at the ingress (load balancer or reverse proxy) for internet-facing listeners; Synapse does not bound message size.

controls.name: Validate or allow-list message-derived destinations
controls.description: Validate or allow-list any destination derived from message content, and avoid a bare <send/> on untrusted traffic unless client-steered routing is intended and network-constrained; restrict egress where transforms may resolve external references.

controls.name: Enable secure processing on transform mediators
controls.description: Per-mediator hardening opt-in: <feature>/<attribute> elements on <xslt> can enable http://javax.xml.XMLConstants/feature/secure-processing. Off by default (JAXP defaults). Do not feed message-derived strings into document()/doc()/extension functions; where unavoidable, enable secure processing on that mediator.

controls.name: Protect the secure-vault keystore and secrets
controls.description: Protect the secure-vault keystore and password, never commit plaintext secrets to configuration, and keep secrets out of log mediators.

controls.name: Keep the pinned Axis2/Axiom builder stack
controls.description: Do not downgrade the pinned Axis2/Axiom builder stack or swap in a builder that permits DOCTYPE; the default DOCTYPE rejection depends on it. Any change to the message-build parser configuration that no longer rejects DOCTYPE invalidates the core parsing property.
